title: The Owl of Tiber Island
synopsis: The Owl wants to meet you at last.
On an old bridge over the river, a familiar face is waiting.
Now the Owl can tell you what really happened.
goal: Meet the Owl, hear the whole week, and see what the real piece shows.

options.label: The bridge with angel statues
options.feedback: This bridge has angels, not stone faces. Read the card again.
options.altText: a long stone bridge with white angel statues along both sides

options.label: The bridge with faces on its posts
options.altText: an old stone bridge with two arches and two stone posts, each with four carved faces

options.label: The bridge with a round hole
options.feedback: This bridge has a round hole, not stone faces. Look for faces on the posts.
options.altText: a stone bridge with a big round hole above its middle arch

notes: A picture choice with the names hidden: the card's words (two stone posts, four faces each, to the island) are matched to what each bridge shows. Real bridges of Rome: Ponte Sant'Angelo (angels), Ponte Sisto (the round hole), Ponte Fabricio (the four-faced posts).
The right picture is the place picture of the mission (tiber_bridge), drawn with nobody on the bridge so it gives nothing away.

clueInputs.note: The bridge card was under the loan book page.

learning.objective: 부엉이 카드의 'two stone posts', 'four faces'를 읽고 세 다리 그림 중 맞는 다리를 고른다.
expressions: the bridge with the stone faces

play.title: The Bridge of Four Heads
story: Rome has many old bridges over the river Tiber.
The Owl's card names only one.
play.letterIntro: The card from the Owl's box says:
play.letter:
Meet me on the bridge with the stone faces.
It goes to the little island in the river.
It has two stone posts. Each post has four faces.
— The Owl
play.question: Which bridge does the Owl mean?
hints: Read the card. What does each post have?
Look closely at each bridge. Which one has faces?
play.successMessage: You found the Bridge of Four Heads!
transition: Two posts, and four stone faces on each one.
On the bridge, a woman in a grey hood is waiting.
She takes off her hood. It is Livia Conti, the restorer!

clue.title: The Owl's Bridge
clue.note: The Owl waited on Ponte Fabricio, the old bridge to Tiber Island.

evidence.name: The Bridge Owl Card
evidence.description: The Owl's card asking to meet on the old bridge.
evidence.inscription: Call out how many faces you see, so I know it is you.

discovery.title: TWO POSTS, EIGHT FACES
discovery.detail: This old bridge goes to Tiber Island. Someone in a hood is waiting there.

options.label: She wanted to sell it.
options.feedback: Livia left the copy for you at the bookshop. Would a seller do that?

options.label: Professor Aldo asked her to.
options.feedback: Read Livia's words again. Who did she tell about the piece?

options.label: So nobody would show a copy and call it real.

notes: Recall: the first owl card (Case 01), to prove Livia is the Owl. Letter: Livia's story.

clueInputs.note: You called out the password, and the Owl turned around.
Livia asks which card she left first.
The plaster copy Livia carried out.
On Saturday, Livia said she was in her lab at midnight (Case 01's talk).

learning.objective: Livia의 이야기에서 행동(복제품을 꺼냄)과 그 이유(so that…)를 연결한다.
expressions: I did not want people to call a copy real.

play.title: The Owl Takes Off Her Hood
story: Livia's hood is down. Her silver owl ring shines.
She looks tired, but she smiles.
play.letter:
"On Friday morning, I cleaned the new piece.
It was wrong! It was too light, and the old crack was gone.
I told Director Sofia. She said, 'You are tired, Livia.'
So at midnight, I turned off the lights and took the piece out.
It was a copy. I did not want people to call a copy real.
I left cards so you could find the truth with your own eyes."
play.question: Why did Livia take the copy out of the glass case?
hints: Livia knew the piece in the case was a copy. What would happen at the show?
Find the line that begins: I did not want...
play.successMessage: Now you know who the Owl is, and why.
transition: Livia took the copy so nobody would call it the real piece.
"Come to my lab," she says. "I wrote down the whole week."

clue.title: The Owl Is Livia
clue.note: Livia saw the piece was a copy. She took it out and left the owl cards.

evidence.name: Livia's Story
evidence.description: What Livia told you on the Bridge of Four Heads.
evidence.inscription: It was too light, and the old crack was gone.

recall.title: Prove it
recall.prompt: Livia asks: which card did I leave for you first?
recall.miss: That is not my first card. Where did your trail begin?

lines.text: On Saturday, you said you worked late.
I did. I was in my lab at midnight.
But first, show me you followed my trail.
I was scared. Nobody believed me.
So I left cards for you.
So I could find the truth myself.

discovery.title: THE OWL IS LIVIA CONTI
discovery.detail: She saw the copy on Friday morning. Nobody believed her, so she acted alone.

options.label: Livia found the piece was too light
Signor Valli took the piece for photos
Signor Valli came to check the lights

notes: Letter: Livia's diary pages, the days out of order. Ordering them shows the swap fell between Tuesday and Friday morning.

clueInputs.note: The loan book page: Tuesday, B.V.

learning.objective: 요일 순서(Tuesday → Thursday → Friday)와 하루 안의 순서(morning → midnight)로 일기를 정리한다.
expressions: On Tuesday, Signor Valli took the piece.
On Thursday night, he came to check the lights.

play.title: Livia's Week
story: Livia's lab is quiet and full of old stones.
She opens her diary on the table.
"The pages fell out," she says. "Can you put them back?"
play.letter:
FRIDAY MORNING — I cleaned the piece. It is light! The crack is gone!
TUESDAY — Signor Valli took the piece out of the lab for poster photos.
FRIDAY, MIDNIGHT — I turned off the lights and took the copy.
THURSDAY NIGHT — Enzo says Signor Valli came at 11 PM to "check the lights".
play.question: Put Livia's week in order.
hints: Say the days: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday.
On Friday, morning comes before midnight.
transition: Tuesday, Thursday night, Friday morning, Friday midnight.
On Friday morning, the piece in the case was already a copy.
"So the swap happened on Thursday night," you say. "When Signor Valli came to check the lights."
play.orderFeedback: Read the days again. Which day comes first in the week?

clue.title: Livia's Week
clue.value: TUE · THU NIGHT · FRI · FRI MIDNIGHT
clue.note: The swap happened on Thursday night, when Valli came to the museum.

evidence.name: Livia's Diary
evidence.description: Livia's diary of the week, put back in order.
evidence.inscription: THURSDAY NIGHT — Signor Valli came at 11 PM to "check the lights".

play.evidenceLinkLine: The loan book page says the same: on Tuesday, B.V. took the piece out.

discovery.title: THE SWAP WAS ON THURSDAY
discovery.detail: On Friday morning, the case already held a copy. Who came on Thursday night?

notes: Letter: Livia's table of the real piece and the copy. The one mark you can see on the real piece and not on the copy: its Y-shaped crack (Aldo's photo).

clueInputs.note: Aldo's photo: a crack shaped like a Y.
By Friday morning the piece was a copy.

learning.objective: 진짜와 복제품의 비교표에서 눈으로 볼 수 있는 차이(crack)를 찾아 글자 타일로 맞춘다.
expressions: The real piece has a crack shaped like a Y.

play.title: Livia's Locker
story: Livia's locker has a letter lock.
"I hid my best clue in here," she says.
"The lock word is the mark only the real piece has."
play.letter:
THE REAL PIECE: marble, 12 kg, a street, an owl, a crack shaped like a Y.
THE COPY: plaster, 4 kg, a street, an owl, no crack.

The lock word: a mark you can see on the real piece. The copy does not have it.
play.question: Spell the mark that only the real piece has.
hints: Both pieces have a long street and a tiny owl.
Look at Aldo's old photo in your Notebook. What shape is the mark?
transition: "I think this room is under Rome today," Livia says.
"And I think Signor Valli knows it."
One man reads old maps like a book: Professor Aldo.
play.orderFeedback: The five tiles fit. What can you see on the real piece?

evidence.name: Livia's Drawing of the Real Piece
evidence.description: Livia drew the real piece from memory, line by line.
evidence.inscription: Next to the tiny owl: a room with shelves, and half a word: BIBLIO...

ending.text: Yes. The crack. Only the real piece has it.

play.caseSummary: The Owl is Livia Conti, the young restorer. She saw the piece was a copy, but nobody believed her. So she took it out and led you to the truth. Her week shows the swap was on Thursday night. Her drawing of the real piece shows a room with shelves: BIBLIO...

notes: Livia's secret ends here (secretUntil, revealCase s3_ep08). Act 2 closes with the swap's night known and its reason still open.
Livia's drawing (s3_ep08_e4) opens Act 3: Case 09 reads the room on it.

STEP 3-14: M1 is now a picture choice of three real Roman bridges (two new pictures and the place's own); the counting password is gone. Livia's talks show her hooded portrait (made in STEP 3-12B) and pay off her Case 01 answer.
